elements.text: Loss of pitch control resulting from the disconnection of the right elevator control tab
Failure to properly secure and inspect the attachment bolt
Bolt connecting the right elevator control tab crank fitting to the pushrod migrated out of the fitting
Control tab disengaged from its pushrod and shifted to a trailing edge down position
Aerodynamic forces restricted the control tab’s further trailing edge up movement, leaving it in an extreme trailing edge down deflection
Right elevator control tab’s extreme trailing edge down deflection drove elevator surfaces to command an extreme nose-up pitch attitude
Pilots were unable to overcome the effects of the restricted right elevator control tab
Captain, first officer, and flight engineer were properly certificated and qualified
No evidence of preexisting medical or behavioral conditions affecting flight crew performance
Accident airplane was certificated, equipped, and dispatched in accordance with regulations
Cargo loading was routine and within prescribed center of gravity limits
Weather and air traffic control were not factors
Improper securement and inspection of the bolt attaching the right elevator control tab crank fitting to the pushrod
DC-8 operators’ procedures and training should emphasize verifying symmetry between elevators and control tabs
DC-8 operators do not use the elevator position indicator (EPI) to confirm elevator movement indications above and below neutral range
Elevator position indicator needs to be periodically calibrated
Elevator position indicator gauge should be readily visible to both pilots
Current DC-8 design does not preclude catastrophic results from disconnection or failure of the control tab crank fitting
Other airplanes certificated to Civil Aviation Regulations 4b standards may be susceptible to catastrophic results from critical flight control disconnection
Replacement of aluminum elevator geared tab crank arms with stainless steel would likely eliminate jamming from fractured arms
DC-8 elevator rigging procedures should be addressed in a separate work card with specific inspection items
DC-8 work cards for critical flight controls should identify required inspection items as discrete tasks with signoff requirements
Air carrier operators should provide maintenance personnel with more detailed information for maintenance tasks
Use of outdated, incomplete, or unsuitable reference materials by maintenance personnel is a potentially unsafe practice
Use of a single FDR parameter correlation for all airplanes of the same type is inadequate for older retrofitted airplanes
Loral Fairchild Model F-800 flight data recorders may have unaddressed tracking-switching anomalies
Current regulatory definition of safety-sensitive functions is too narrow for postaccident testing
